title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an abstract, combinatorial axiomatics for 'analysis situs'. The data are 'lieux' (places) organised into 'ateliers' (workshops) and 'atlas'. On the previous pages he goes the other way: from abstract data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) he builds an atelier satisfying At1–At7. He then checks (Lemmas 6–7) that the structure recovered from it is the one he started with.

Notation, inferred from the surrounding pages:
- L is the set of ≪-minimal elements of M (the 'points', or atoms).
- omb(X), the 'ombre' (shadow) of X, is the set of x ∈ L with x ≪ X. The machine transcription renders it 'amb' or 'ens'.
- X̃ is the corresponding underlying set of X.
- X ≭ Y is a compatibility relation. Lemma 7a says that for points, x ≭ y iff x = y or x ‖ y. So ≭ plausibly means 'nested or disjoint', as in a laminar family.
- ‖ is disjointness.

Lemma 8 (this page). For X, Y ∈ M: (X ≭ Y and X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅) ⇔ (for all x ∈ omb(X) and y ∈ omb(Y), x ‖ y). In words, X ‖ Y in the sense of the atlas. Grothendieck remarks 'C'est tautologique !': disjointness of lieux is defined pointwise from disjointness of points. This is the place axiom AtL2.

Conclusion drawn. The atlas constructed from the abstract data satisfies At1–At7 and the place axioms AtL1, AtL2, AtL3. The remaining condition AtCL(spec) holds by definition.

The page then opens a 'Théorème-Scholie', a representation/characterisation theorem:
- Hypotheses: (M, ≤, ≪) is a set with two order relations, L is the set of ≪-minimal elements, and ‖ is a symmetric antireflexive relation on L.
- Claim: these data are isomorphic to the data coming from an (optimal) atlas satisfying At1–At7, AtL1–AtL3 and AtCL(spec) iff the conditions ML0–ML5 hold.
- ML0–ML5 are stated on the next page. They say: ≤ implies ≪; a lifting/'suffisance' axiom; every X has a point in its interior omb(X)°; every point under X is interior to some X' ≤ X; ‖ is symmetric antireflexive; and points of X outside Y ≤ X are disjoint from points of Y.

The problem served is an intrinsic characterisation of the combinatorial skeleton of 'spaces of places' (the 'lieux' structures). It belongs to Grothendieck's search for a non-pointlike, combinatorial foundation of topology, in line with the 'topologie modérée' programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Lemma 8 is indeed tautological, provided disjointness of lieux and X̃ are defined pointwise via omb. The 'or more' insertion in the theorem's hypotheses is garbled, and the precise meaning of ≭ and X̃ cannot be fixed from this page alone.
The theorem statement is left syntactically unfinished on this page (duplicated line 'par ≪ ... anti-', several overwritten insertions); the content continues on p. 34.

ideas.what: Disjointness of composite places defined pointwise from disjointness of minimal places (Lemma 8 / AtL2)
ideas.modern_name: pointwise/atomic definition of disjointness in a mereological lattice; 'discrete from' relation in mereotopology

ideas.what: Théorème-Scholie: an axiomatic characterisation (ML0–ML5) of the poset data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) arising from optimal atlases of places, with points as ≪-minimal elements
ideas.modern_name: representation theorem for abstract region/place structures; close to point-free topology and region-based (mereotopological) theories of space, and to combinatorial models of stratified/cellular spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; related work by Whitehead (1929), Tarski (geometry of solids), Clarke (1981), de Vries (compingent algebras), and RCC by Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of a 'tame topology' is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; the 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics have several features of region-based (mereotopological) theories of space developed independently in philosophy, logic and AI: places with an order, minimal elements as points, a disjointness relation, and an interior notion omb(X)°. The analogue would be Clarke's calculus or RCC, where points are recovered as minimal or ideal regions. This link is not made in the literature on Grothendieck's tame topology.
missed.quote: Soit (M, ≤, ≪) un ensemble muni de deux relations d'ordre, L l'ens des éléments minimaux de M par ≪, ‖ une relation symétrique antiréflexive sur L.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a representation theorem of the kind sought in point-free topology and qualitative spatial reasoning. It also gives a concrete entry point for reconstructing Grothendieck's unpublished 'analysis situs' programme.

missed.claim: The full axiomatic programme (At1–At7, AtL1–AtL3, AtCL(spec), ML0–ML5) and its equivalence theorem appear never to have been written up or studied. Its relation to tame topology and stratified spaces is left implicit.
missed.quote: Pour que ces données soient isom. à celles provenant d'un atlas optimal satisfaisant ... il faut & suffit que les conditions suivantes soient satisfaites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the open problem of a combinatorial foundation of 'topologie modérée', as alternatives to o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine verification ('C'est tautologique !') plus the statement of a characterisation theorem. Its interest lies in documenting an unpublished axiomatic theory of 'lieux' and atlases with its own representation theorem. That theory is essentially absent from the literature, but this page adds little beyond its statement.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 of Lemma 8: 'X ≪̸ Y' should read 'X ≭ Y' (same compatibility symbol as $X \not\asymp Y$ on p. 32).
'∀ x ∈ ens(X), y ∈ ens(Y)' is probably '∀ x ∈ omb(X), y ∈ omb(Y)' (ombre), consistent with p. 34. On p. 32, 'amb' likewise should be 'omb'.
'L l'ens des éléments minimaux de M' continues 'par ≪' on the next line; the line 'par ≪, ‖ une relation symétrique anti-' is duplicated in the machine transcription.
'soient {+issues+} à celui provenant' should be read as 'soient isom. à celles provenant d'un atlas optimal'. The insertion above 'soient' is 'isom.'.
'(ou plus à At1–At7)' is probably '(en plus de At1–At7)'.
'Lemme 9' is struck out before 'Ainsi, un tel atlas satisfait'.
